```{r data_part1, include=FALSE}
# ---- game QR codes: use the game's own images when they exist, else the copies in this folder ----
qr_path = function(s) {
  p = file.path("../../games/game-day/images", paste0("qr_", s, ".png"))
  if (file.exists(p)) p else paste0("qr_", s, ".png")
}
stopifnot(file.exists(qr_path("A")), file.exists(qr_path("B")))

# ---- Notes From Wednesday ----
# 1. Fox News chart: Pew Research Center values (77% in 2009, 65% in 2018/2019)
fox = list(old = 77, new = 65)
fox$pts = fox$old - fox$new                 # percentage points
fox$pct = 100 * (fox$old - fox$new) / fox$old  # percent decline
stopifnot(fox$pts == 12, round(fox$pct, 1) == 15.6)

# 2. Playfair's cities: London vs Constantinople in the class CSV
playfair = readr::read_csv("../../data/playfair_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
pf_london = playfair$population[playfair$city == "London"]
pf_const = playfair$population[playfair$city == "Constantinople"]
stopifnot(length(pf_london) == 1, length(pf_const) == 1,
          pf_london == 1100, pf_const == 900, pf_london > pf_const,
          playfair$city[which.max(playfair$population)] == "London")

# 3. Fox chart crop (the chart only, without the studio), for the axis-on-the-right note
fox_crop = file.path(tempdir(), "fox_chart_crop.png")
magick::image_read("../../figures/terrible_fox_christian.jpg") |>
  magick::image_crop("950x545+425+62") |>
  magick::image_resize("700x") |>
  magick::image_write(fox_crop, format = "png")
stopifnot(file.exists(fox_crop))

# ---- data terminology activity ----
shipping_data = readr::read_csv("../../data/shipping_data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(trimws) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(dplyr::where(is.character), trimws))

# ---- color vision deficiency figure (same as deck 15) ----
pal_rg = c(Adelie = "#D7191C", Chinstrap = "#1A9641", Gentoo = "#A6611A")
pal_oi = c(Adelie = "#E69F00", Chinstrap = "#56B4E9", Gentoo = "#009E73")

peng = datasets::penguins |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(bill_len), !is.na(flipper_len))

cvd = tidyr::expand_grid(
  palette = factor(c("Red / green palette", "Okabe-Ito palette"), levels = c("Red / green palette", "Okabe-Ito palette")),
  vision = factor(c("Typical color vision", "Simulated deuteranopia"), levels = c("Typical color vision", "Simulated deuteranopia"))) |>
  dplyr::cross_join(peng) |>
  dplyr::mutate(col = ifelse(palette == "Red / green palette", pal_rg[as.character(species)], pal_oi[as.character(species)]),
                col = ifelse(vision == "Simulated deuteranopia", colorspace::deutan(col), col))

cvd_lab = cvd |>
  dplyr::group_by(palette, vision, species, col) |>
  dplyr::summarise(bill_len = mean(bill_len), flipper_len = mean(flipper_len), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(flipper_len = flipper_len + c(Adelie = -14, Chinstrap = 14, Gentoo = 13)[as.character(species)])

cvd_file = file.path(tempdir(), "cvd_penguins.png")
cvd_plot = ggplot2::ggplot(cvd, ggplot2::aes(bill_len, flipper_len)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = col), size = 1.1, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggplot2::geom_label(data = cvd_lab, ggplot2::aes(label = species, color = col), size = 2.8, fontface = "bold", linewidth = 0.3) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_identity() +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(palette ~ vision) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Bill length (mm)", y = "Flipper length (mm)") +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 10)
ggplot2::ggsave(cvd_file, cvd_plot, width = 6.4, height = 4.2, dpi = 220)
stopifnot(file.exists(cvd_file))
```

.sc-btn:disabled { opacity:0.4; cursor:default; }
.sc-btn.sc-primary { background:#c3142d; color:#ffffff; border-color:#c3142d; }
.sc-spds { display:inline-flex; border:1px solid #d1d5db; border-radius:6px; overflow:hidden; margin-left:4px; }
.sc-spd { background:#ffffff; color:#374151; border:0; border-right:1px solid #d1d5db; padding:4px 8px; font-size:11.5px; cursor:pointer; }
.sc-spd:last-child { border-right:0; }
.sc-spd.on { background:#585E60; color:#ffffff; }
.sc-count { margin-left:auto; color:#585E60; font-size:12px; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; }
.sc-caps { position:relative; margin-top:8px; border:1px solid #d1d5db; border-left:5px solid #c3142d; border-radius:8px; background:#fdf2f2; padding:8px 12px; font-size:13.5px; line-height:1.45; color:#1b1b1b; min-height:46px; }
.sc-cap { display:none; }
.sc-cap.on { display:block; }
.sc-cap b { color:#c3142d; }
</style>
<script>
(function () {
  if (window.isaStepper) { return; }
  window.isaStepper = function (root, scene) {
    if (root.getAttribute('data-built')) { return; }
    root.setAttribute('data-built', '1');
    var i = 0, timer = null, speed = 1;
    var q = function (s) { return root.querySelector(s); };
    var bBack = q('.sc-back'), bStep = q('.sc-step'), bPlay = q('.sc-play'), bReset = q('.sc-reset'), cnt = q('.sc-count');
    var spd = root.querySelectorAll('.sc-spd');
    var caps = root.querySelectorAll('.sc-cap');
    var flagged = root.querySelectorAll('[data-from]');
    function applyFlags(j) {
      flagged.forEach(function (el) {
        var f = Number(el.getAttribute('data-from'));
        var t = el.hasAttribute('data-to') ? Number(el.getAttribute('data-to')) : 9999;
        el.classList.toggle('on', j >= f && !(j >= t));
      });
      caps.forEach(function (c) { c.classList.toggle('on', Number(c.getAttribute('data-step')) === j); });
    }
    function paint() {
      bBack.disabled = (i === 0);
      bStep.disabled = (i === scene.n);
      bPlay.textContent = (timer !== null) ? 'Pause' : 'Play';
      cnt.textContent = i + ' / ' + scene.n;
    }
    function go(j, dir) { i = j; applyFlags(j); if (scene.render) { scene.render(j, dir, speed, root); } paint(); }
    function stop() { if (timer !== null) { clearTimeout(timer); timer = null; } paint(); }
    function tick() {
      timer = null;
      if (i === scene.n) { paint(); return; }
      go(i + 1, 1);
      if (i !== scene.n) { timer = setTimeout(tick, scene.dwell[i] / speed); }
      paint();
    }
    bStep.addEventListener('click', function () { stop(); if (i !== scene.n) { go(i + 1, 1); } });
    bBack.addEventListener('click', function () { stop(); if (i !== 0) { go(i - 1, -1); } });
    bReset.addEventListener('click', function () { stop(); go(0, -1); });
    bPlay.addEventListener('click', function () {
      if (timer !== null) { stop(); return; }
      if (i === scene.n) { go(0, -1); }
      timer = setTimeout(tick, scene.dwell[i] / speed);
      paint();
    });
    spd.forEach(function (b) {
      b.addEventListener('click', function () {
        speed = Number(b.getAttribute('data-spd'));
        spd.forEach(function (o) { o.classList.toggle('on', o === b); });
      });
    });
    ['keydown', 'keypress', 'keyup'].forEach(function (t) { root.addEventListener(t, function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); });
    root.addEventListener('mousedown', function (e) { if (e.target.tagName === 'BUTTON') { e.preventDefault(); } });
    root.addEventListener('focusin', function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.pause(); } });
    root.addEventListener('focusout', function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.resume(); } });
    if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.on('hideSlide', stop); }
    go(0, -1);
  };
  window.isaTypewriter = function (el, text, msPerChar, done) {
    var k = 0, h = null;
    function step() {
      k = k + 1;
      el.textContent = text.slice(0, k);
      if (k !== text.length) { h = setTimeout(step, msPerChar); } else { h = null; if (done) { done(); } }
    }
    el.textContent = '';
    h = setTimeout(step, msPerChar);
    return function () { if (h !== null) { clearTimeout(h); h = null; } };
  };
})();
</script>

3. **Refine** charts with labels, scales, and themes.

4. **Critique** and improve draft visualizations.

# Notes From Wednesday

<div style="display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:14px; margin-top:12px;">
<div style="display:flex; flex-direction:column; gap:14px;">
<div class="card"><div class="ch">1 &nbsp; Correction: points vs. percent</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.5;">
<div>Christians in the US: `r fox$old`% (2009) to `r fox$new`% (2018/2019).</div>
<div class="eq" style="font-size:17px; margin:8px 0;"><span class="frac"><span class="ft">`r fox$old` &minus; `r fox$new`</span><span class="fb">`r fox$old`</span></span><span>=</span><span class="res">`r formatC(fox$pct, format = "f", digits = 1)`% decline</span></div>
<div>The drop is <b>`r fox$pts` percentage points</b>, which is a <b>`r formatC(fox$pct, format = "f", digits = 1)`% decline</b>. Our typed note on the Fox slide said "12% drop".</div>
<div class="src" style="margin-top:6px;">Values: <a href="https://www.pewresearch.org/religion/2019/10/17/in-u-s-decline-of-christianity-continues-at-rapid-pace/" target="_blank">Pew Research Center (2019)</a>.</div>
</div></div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch">2 &nbsp; Correction: Playfair's largest city</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.5;">
<div>In our Playfair data, <b>London (`r scales::comma(pf_london)`K)</b> is larger than <b>Constantinople (`r scales::comma(pf_const)`K)</b>. London is the largest of the `r nrow(playfair)` cities.</div>
<div class="src" style="margin-top:6px;">Data: <code>data/playfair_data.csv</code>, from <a href="http://www.stat.uiowa.edu/~luke/data/Playfair" target="_blank">stat.uiowa.edu/~luke/data/Playfair</a>.</div>
</div></div>
</div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch gray">3 &nbsp; Promised: where is the Fox chart's y-axis?</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:14.5px; line-height:1.5;">
<img src="`r knitr::image_uri(fox_crop)`" alt="The Fox News bar chart of Americans who identify as Christians, with y-axis labels 58, 68, and 78 on the right side" style="display:block; width:100%; border-radius:4px;">
<div style="margin-top:8px;">The y-axis labels (<b>58, 68, 78</b>) are on the <b>right</b> side of the chart. The axis starts at 58, not 0, so the 2019 bar looks less than half as tall as the 2009 bar.</div>

# Data Types in One Slide

<div class="dt-grp"><div style="border-bottom:none;"></div><div class="r">QUANTITATIVE</div></div>

<div class="dt4">
<div class="card"><div class="ch gray">Nominal</div><div class="cb">Values are only <b>=</b> or <b>&ne;</b>.<div class="ex">Apples, bananas, oranges; jersey numbers.</div><div class="test"><b>Test:</b> is jersey #22 "twice" jersey #11? <b>No.</b> The number is a label.</div></div></div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch gray">Ordinal</div><div class="cb">Values have an order (<b>&lt;</b>), but the gaps are not equal amounts.<div class="ex">Survey ratings (poor, fair, good); finishing place (1st, 2nd, 3rd).</div><div class="test"><b>Test:</b> is the gap from 1st to 2nd place the same as from 2nd to 3rd? <b>We cannot say.</b></div></div></div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch">Interval</div><div class="cb">Differences mean something; the location of zero is arbitrary.<div class="ex">Temperature in &deg;F or &deg;C.</div><div class="test r"><b>Test:</b> is 40&deg;F twice as warm as 20&deg;F? <b>No,</b> but the 20&deg;F difference is meaningful.</div></div></div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch">Ratio</div><div class="cb">Zero means none, so ratios, proportions, and differences all mean something.<div class="ex">Length, weight, counts.</div><div class="test r"><b>Test:</b> is a 40 lb bag twice as heavy as a 20 lb bag? <b>Yes.</b> 0 lb means no weight.</div></div></div>
</div>

<div class="lesson" style="margin-top:16px;"><b class="r">Why it matters for charts:</b> a bar's length shows a value as a distance from zero. That works for ratio data. For interval data, a bar from zero has no meaning, so we use positions (dots, lines) instead.</div>

<div class="src" style="margin-top:8px;">Source: Stevens, S. S. (1946). <a href="https://doi.org/10.1126/science.103.2684.677" target="_blank">On the Theory of Scales of Measurement</a>. <i>Science</i>, 103(2684), 677-680.</div>

<tr><td>Product Container</td><td>Nominal or ordinal</td><td>Small, medium, large, and jumbo box have an order, so ordinal can be argued. A wrap bag has no place in that order, so with it in the column, nominal is the safer answer.</td></tr>

Both answers for Product Container are accepted (that matches what was said in Section A on Wednesday). For the dates, "interval" is the precise answer and "quantitative" is accepted. # Data vs. Conceptual Models

<div style="display:flex; gap:12px; align-items:stretch; margin-top:18px;">
<div class="card" style="flex:1;"><div class="ch gray">1 &nbsp; Data model</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:16px; line-height:1.7;">32.5, 54.0, &minus;17.3, ...<div style="color:#585E60; font-size:14px;">Numbers in a column.</div></div></div>
<div style="align-self:center; color:#c3142d; font-size:24px; font-weight:700;">&rarr;</div>
<div class="card" style="flex:1;"><div class="ch gray">2 &nbsp; Conceptual model</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:16px; line-height:1.7;">Temperature<div style="color:#585E60; font-size:14px;">What the numbers mean.</div></div></div>
<div style="align-self:center; color:#c3142d; font-size:24px; font-weight:700;">&rarr;</div>
<div class="card" style="flex:1.4;"><div class="ch">3 &nbsp; Data type we choose</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:15.5px; line-height:1.7;">
<div>Continuous to x significant digits: <b>quantitative</b></div>
<div>Hot, warm, cold: <b>ordinal</b></div>
<div>Burned vs. not burned: <b>nominal</b></div>
</div></div>
</div>

<div class="lesson" style="margin-top:18px;"><b class="r">The same column can become different data types,</b> depending on the question we ask. The type we choose decides which visual encodings fit.</div>

# Visual Channels and Their Precision

class: inverse, center, middle

# Part 2: The Grammar of Graphics

```{r data_part2, include=FALSE}
# ---- Part 2: the grammar of graphics ----
# Every stepper figure is made by running the exact code string shown on the slide (minus the #<< marker),
# so the code on the slide and the picture next to it cannot drift apart. Steps before a theme layer
# use ggplot2's real default theme (theme_grey), not the deck's theme_bw.
p2_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "part2")
dir.create(p2_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
p2_file = function(name) file.path(p2_dir, paste0(name, ".png"))

# eval() only runs the code strings written in this chunk (never outside input).
gg_run = function(code, name, w = 4.6, h = 3.6, env = globalenv()) {
  code = gsub("#<<", "", paste(code, collapse = "\n"), fixed = TRUE)
  old = ggplot2::theme_set(ggplot2::theme_grey())
  on.exit(ggplot2::theme_set(old))
  p = eval(parse(text = code), envir = env)
  ggplot2::ggsave(p2_file(name), p, width = w, height = h, dpi = 200)
  stopifnot(file.exists(p2_file(name)))
  p2_file(name)
}

# Line up the layer-name comments (# data, # aesthetics, ...) in one column: the same column on every
# step of a stepper, so the comments do not move between steps.
cm_re = "^(.*?\\S)\\s+(# [a-z][a-z :]*(?: #<<)?)\\s*$"
cm_width = function(codes) {
  l = unlist(strsplit(unlist(codes), "\n", fixed = TRUE))
  l = l[grepl(cm_re, l, perl = TRUE)]
  if (!length(l)) return(0)
  max(nchar(sub(cm_re, "\\1", l, perl = TRUE))) + 2
}
align_comments = function(code, w = cm_width(code)) {
  l = strsplit(code, "\n", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  has = grepl(cm_re, l, perl = TRUE)
  l[has] = paste0(formatC(sub(cm_re, "\\1", l[has], perl = TRUE), width = -w), sub(cm_re, "\\2", l[has], perl = TRUE))
  paste(l, collapse = "\n")
}

# Stepper HTML: code (left) and figure (right) for each step, a caption below, then the controls.
# steps: list of list(code = <string or NULL>, fig = <png path or raw HTML>, alt = , cap = <HTML>)
# ratio: width / height of the figures, so the figure box keeps one size on every step.
ggs = function(steps, dwell, size = "60%", ratio = "4.6 / 3.6", note0 = "") {
  n = length(steps) - 1
  w = cm_width(lapply(steps, function(s) s$code))
  code_div = vapply(seq_along(steps), function(k) {
    s = steps[[k]]
    inner = if (is.null(s$code)) paste0("<div class='ggs-empty'>", note0, "</div>") else hl_r(align_comments(s$code, w), size)
    sprintf("<div class='ggs-v' data-from='%d' data-to='%d'>%s</div>", k - 1, k, inner)
  }, "")
  fig_div = vapply(seq_along(steps), function(k) {
    s = steps[[k]]
    inner = if (grepl("\\.png$", s$fig)) sprintf("<img src='%s' alt='%s'>", knitr::image_uri(s$fig), s$alt) else s$fig
    sprintf("<div class='ggs-v' data-from='%d' data-to='%d'>%s</div>", k - 1, k, inner)
  }, "")
  caps = vapply(seq_along(steps), function(k) {
    sprintf("<div class='sc-cap%s' data-step='%d'>%s</div>", if (k == 1) " on" else "", k - 1, steps[[k]]$cap)
  }, "")
  bar = paste0("<div class='sc-bar'><button type='button' class='sc-btn sc-back'>Back</button>",
               "<button type='button' class='sc-btn sc-primary sc-step'>Step</button>",
               "<button type='button' class='sc-btn sc-play'>Play</button>",
               "<button type='button' class='sc-btn sc-reset'>Reset</button>",
               "<span class='sc-spds'><button type='button' class='sc-spd' data-spd='0.5'>0.5x</button>",
               "<button type='button' class='sc-spd on' data-spd='1'>1x</button>",
               "<button type='button' class='sc-spd' data-spd='2'>2x</button></span>",
               "<span class='sc-count'>0 / ", n, "</span></div>")
  stopifnot(length(dwell) == n + 1)
  paste0("<div class='ggs' data-n='", n, "' data-dwell='", paste(dwell, collapse = ","), "'>",
         "<div class='ggs-grid'><div class='ggs-l'>", paste(code_div, collapse = ""), "</div>",
         "<div class='ggs-r' style='aspect-ratio:", ratio, ";'>", paste(fig_div, collapse = ""), "</div></div>",
         "<div class='sc-caps ggs-caps'>", paste(caps, collapse = ""), "</div>", bar, "</div>")
}

# Playfair's cities plus a region column. Playfair's data has no region, so we derive one:
# the UN M49 subregion of each city's present-day country (https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/m49/).
# Istanbul (Constantinople) is in Turkiye, which M49 places in Western Asia.
m49 = c(London = "Northern Europe", Constantinople = "Western Asia", Paris = "Western Europe",
        Naples = "Southern Europe", Vienna = "Western Europe", Moscow = "Eastern Europe",
        Amsterdam = "Western Europe", Dublin = "Northern Europe", Venice = "Southern Europe",
        Petersburgh = "Eastern Europe", Rome = "Southern Europe", Berlin = "Western Europe",
        Madrid = "Southern Europe", Palermo = "Southern Europe", Lisbon = "Southern Europe",
        Copenhagen = "Northern Europe", Genoa = "Southern Europe", Turin = "Southern Europe",
        Warsaw = "Eastern Europe", Florence = "Southern Europe", Stockholm = "Northern Europe",
        Edinburgh = "Northern Europe")
stopifnot(setequal(names(m49), playfair$city), nrow(playfair) == 22)
playfair = playfair |> dplyr::mutate(region = unname(m49[city]))

region_totals = playfair |>
  dplyr::group_by(region) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cities = dplyr::n(), population = sum(population), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(population))
stopifnot(sum(region_totals$cities) == 22, sum(region_totals$population) == sum(playfair$population))

# the finding stated in the Playfair title
pf_big = playfair$city[playfair$population > 500]
stopifnot(length(pf_big) == 3, setequal(pf_big, c("London", "Constantinople", "Paris")))

# ---- slide: The Grammar of Graphics (stacked bar -> pie) ----
region_totals = region_totals |> dplyr::mutate(region = forcats::fct_inorder(region))
code_bar = 'ggplot2::ggplot(data = region_totals,        # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = "", y = population,       # aesthetics
    fill = region)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +                      # geometry
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates
  ggplot2::theme_void()                      # theme'
code_pie = sub("  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates",
               '  ggplot2::coord_polar(theta = "y") +        # coordinates #<<', code_bar, fixed = TRUE)
stopifnot(code_pie != code_bar)
f_bar = gg_run(code_bar, "s13_bar")
f_pie = gg_run(code_pie, "s13_pie")
s13_table = paste0("<div class='tbl-sm ggs-tbl'>",
                   tbl(region_totals |> dplyr::mutate(population = scales::comma(population)) |>
                         dplyr::rename(`population (thousands)` = population),
                       align = c("l", "r", "r")), "</div>")

# ---- slide: Building Playfair's Cities (data -> aes -> geom -> reorder -> labs -> theme) ----
# step 0 is Playfair's bubble chart from Wednesday, redrawn in four rows so the city names are legible
pf_bubble = playfair |>
  dplyr::mutate(row = rep(1:4, times = c(6, 6, 5, 5)),
                col = c(1:6, 1:6, 1:5, 1:5),
                lab = paste0(city, "\n", scales::comma(population), "K"))
f_bubble = file.path(p2_dir, "s16_bubble.png")
ggplot2::ggsave(f_bubble, width = 4.6, height = 3.6, dpi = 200, plot =
  ggplot2::ggplot(pf_bubble, ggplot2::aes(x = col, y = -row)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(size = population), shape = 21, fill = "white", color = "grey25") +
    ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = lab), size = 2.5, lineheight = 0.85, nudge_y = 0.48) +
    ggplot2::scale_size_area(max_size = 16) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = c(0.45, 0.65))) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(add = 0.6)) +
    ggplot2::theme_void() + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none"))

pf_title = "Only three cities had over 500,000 people"
pf_code = list(
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair)             # data #<<',
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics #<<
    y = city))',
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics
    y = city)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point()                      # geometry #<<',
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics
    y = forcats::fct_reorder(city, population))) + #<<
  ggplot2::geom_point()                      # geometry',
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics
    y = forcats::fct_reorder(city, population))) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +                    # geometry
  ggplot2::labs(                             # labels #<<
    title = "Only three cities had over 500,000 people",
    x = "Population (thousands)", y = NULL)',
'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics
    y = forcats::fct_reorder(city, population))) +
  ggplot2::geom_point() +                    # geometry
  ggplot2::labs(                             # labels
    title = "Only three cities had over 500,000 people",
    x = "Population (thousands)", y = NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw()                        # theme #<<')
stopifnot(grepl(pf_title, pf_code[[6]], fixed = TRUE))
f_pf = vapply(seq_along(pf_code), function(k) gg_run(pf_code[[k]], paste0("s16_", k)), "")

# ---- slide: Mapping vs Setting (starts from the finished Playfair chart) ----
pf_final = gsub(" #<<", "", pf_code[[6]], fixed = TRUE)
geom_line_txt = "  ggplot2::geom_point() +                    # geometry"
stopifnot(grepl(geom_line_txt, pf_final, fixed = TRUE))
swap_geom = function(new) { out = sub(geom_line_txt, new, pf_final, fixed = TRUE); stopifnot(out != pf_final); out }
ms_code = list(
  pf_final,
  swap_geom('  ggplot2::geom_point(                       # geometry #<<
    ggplot2::aes(color = region)) +'),
  swap_geom('  ggplot2::geom_point(                       # geometry
    ggplot2::aes(color = region)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_brewer(palette = "Dark2") + # scales #<<'),
  swap_geom('  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "#C3142D") +   # geometry #<<'),
  swap_geom('  ggplot2::geom_point(                       # geometry #<<
    ggplot2::aes(color = "#C3142D")) +'))
f_ms = vapply(seq_along(ms_code), function(k) gg_run(ms_code[[k]], paste0("s17_", k)), "")

# ---- slide: Change One Layer (each step changes one line of the step-1 chart) ----
col_base = 'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair,             # data
  ggplot2::aes(x = population,               # aesthetics
    y = forcats::fct_reorder(city, population))) +
  ggplot2::geom_col() +                      # geometry
  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Population (thousands)", y = NULL)'
col_swap = function(old, new) { out = sub(old, new, col_base, fixed = TRUE); stopifnot(out != col_base); out }
cl_code = list(
  col_base,
  col_swap("  ggplot2::geom_col() +                      # geometry",
           "  ggplot2::geom_point() +                    # geometry #<<"),
  col_swap("  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates",
           '  ggplot2::coord_radial(theta = "y") +       # coordinates #<<'),
  col_swap("  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates",
           '  ggplot2::coord_cartesian() +               # coordinates
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ region, ncol = 2,    # facets #<<
    scales = "free_y") +'))
f_cl = vapply(seq_along(cl_code), function(k) gg_run(cl_code[[k]], paste0("s18_", k), w = 5.6, h = 4.24), "")

st = function(code, fig, alt, cap) list(code = code, fig = fig, alt = alt, cap = cap)

s13_html = ggs(list(
  st(NULL, s13_table, "", "<b>The data:</b> the total population of Playfair's 22 cities in each region. A chart menu, as in Excel, offers a fixed list of chart types. The grammar of graphics describes a chart by its parts instead."),
  st(code_bar, f_bar, "A single stacked bar of population by region",
     "<b>A stacked bar.</b> Data, an aesthetic mapping (fill = region), a geometry (columns), and Cartesian coordinates."),
  st(code_pie, f_pie, "The same data as a pie chart",
     "<b>A pie.</b> Only the coordinates line changed. coord_polar() wraps the same bar around a circle: a pie chart is a stacked bar in polar coordinates.")),
  dwell = c(3000, 5000, 0), size = "62%", note0 = "The code appears on Step 1.")

s16_html = ggs(list(
  st(NULL, f_bubble, "Playfair's bubble chart of 22 cities, redrawn",

  st(pf_code[[1]], f_pf[1], "An empty gray canvas",
     "<b>Data.</b> ggplot() gets the table but no mappings, so it draws an empty canvas."),
  st(pf_code[[2]], f_pf[2], "Axes for population and city, with nothing plotted",
     "<b>Aesthetics.</b> Population goes to the x position and city to the y position. The axes appear, but nothing is drawn: there is no geometry yet."),
  st(pf_code[[3]], f_pf[3], "One point per city, cities in alphabetical order",
     "<b>Geometry.</b> geom_point() draws one point per row (22 cities). The cities are in alphabetical order, so the ranking is hard to read."),
  st(pf_code[[4]], f_pf[4], "The same points with cities sorted by population",
     "<b>Reorder.</b> fct_reorder() sorts the cities by population. This changes the y aesthetic; the data are unchanged."),
  st(pf_code[[5]], f_pf[5], "The sorted dot chart with a title and an x-axis label",
     "<b>Labels.</b> The title states the finding. The x-axis label gives the unit, and y = NULL removes the y-axis title, which showed the code."),
  st(pf_code[[6]], f_pf[6], "The finished dot chart with a white background",
     "<b>Theme.</b> theme_bw() changes the parts that do not show data: a white background and gray grid lines. This is the dot chart behind Wednesday's My Solution tab.")),
  dwell = c(3000, 4500, 5500, 5500, 5500, 5500, 0), size = "60%", note0 = "The code appears on Step 1.")

s17_html = ggs(list(
  st(ms_code[[1]], f_ms[1], "The finished Playfair dot chart in black",
     "<b>The chart we just built.</b> There are two ways to give the points a color: map a variable to color, or set one color for all points."),
  st(ms_code[[2]], f_ms[2], "Points colored by region with a legend",
     "<b>Mapping.</b> Inside aes(), color = region maps a nominal variable to color. ggplot2 picks one color per region and adds a legend."),
  st(ms_code[[3]], f_ms[3], "Points colored by region with the Dark2 palette",
     "<b>Scales.</b> scale_color_brewer() uses a ColorBrewer qualitative palette (Dark2), which suits a nominal variable such as region."),
  st(ms_code[[4]], f_ms[4], "All points in Miami red, no legend",
     "<b>Setting.</b> Outside aes(), color = \"#C3142D\" gives every point the same color. No variable is involved, so there is no legend."),
  st(ms_code[[5]], f_ms[5], "All points in a pinkish red with a legend that reads #C3142D",
     "<b>A common mistake.</b> Inside aes(), \"#C3142D\" is treated as data: a variable with one value. ggplot2 colors that value with its first default color (not Miami red) and adds a legend.")),
  dwell = c(3500, 5500, 5000, 5000, 0), size = "56%")

s18_html = ggs(list(

  st(cl_code[[2]], f_cl[2], "Points of population by city",
```

# The Grammar of Graphics

`r s13_html`

<script>
(function () {
  function buildGgs() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.ggs, .lyrs').forEach(function (root) {
      var d = root.getAttribute('data-dwell').split(',').map(Number);
      window.isaStepper(root, { n: Number(root.getAttribute('data-n')), dwell: d });
    });
  }
  buildGgs();
  if (window.slideshow) { if (!window.ggsHooked) { window.ggsHooked = true; window.slideshow.on('afterShowSlide', buildGgs); } }
})();
</script>

<div class="src" style="margin-top:6px;">Data: <code>data/playfair_data.csv</code>. The region column is ours, not Playfair's: the <a href="https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/m49/" target="_blank">UN M49</a> subregion of each city's present-day country (Istanbul is in Türkiye, which M49 places in Western Asia).</div>

???

Two minutes (15 to 17). Step 0: Excel and Tableau start from a menu of chart types. The grammar starts from parts. Step 1: name the parts out loud: data, aesthetic (fill = region), geometry (columns), coordinates. Step 2: only the coordinates line changed and the bar became a pie. The aes(x = "") is a one-value variable on purpose: it puts all five regions in one bar, which coord_polar() turns into one pie. That is the idea for the next 20 minutes: a chart is a sentence made of parts, and changing one part gives a different chart. The region column was added by us (UN M49 subregions), as the source line says.

<div class="sc-cap" data-step="1">`r lyr_cap(1, '<b>Data.</b> Which table is the chart made from, and what is one row? Here, one row is one city.', 'ggplot2::ggplot(data = playfair)')`</div>
<div class="sc-cap" data-step="2">`r lyr_cap(2, '<b>Aesthetics.</b> Which column goes to which visual channel: x position, y position, color, size, shape. Scales then set how each mapping is drawn (which colors, which axis breaks).', 'ggplot2::aes(x = population, y = city)')`</div>
<div class="sc-cap" data-step="3">`r lyr_cap(3, '<b>Geometries.</b> The marks that show the data: points, lines, bars, text.', 'ggplot2::geom_point()')`</div>

<div class="sc-cap" data-step="6">`r lyr_cap(6, '<b>Coordinates.</b> The space the marks are drawn in: Cartesian (x and y), polar (angle and radius), or a map projection.', 'ggplot2::coord_radial(theta = \"y\")')`</div>

<div class="src" style="margin-top:8px;">Sources: Wilkinson, L. (2005). <a href="https://doi.org/10.1007/0-387-28695-0" target="_blank"><i>The Grammar of Graphics</i></a> (2nd ed.). Springer. Wickham, H. (2010). <a href="https://doi.org/10.1198/jcgs.2009.07098" target="_blank">A Layered Grammar of Graphics</a>. <i>Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics</i>, 19(1), 3-28. The seven-layer stack is a common teaching summary of these papers; "theme" is ggplot2's name for the non-data parts.</div>

???

Two and a half minutes (17 to 19.5). Step through the seven layers from the bottom. Only the first three are required for every chart; the other four have defaults (no facets, no statistic beyond the identity, Cartesian coordinates, the gray theme). Wilkinson wrote the grammar; Wickham's layered version is what ggplot2 implements. Tableau and Power BI use the same ideas: their shelves and wells are the aesthetics.

Three and a half minutes (20.5 to 24). Section B never saw Wednesday's My Solution tab; this is it, built one layer at a time. Step 0: the bubble chart from the activity. Before each Step, ask the room what the next layer will change. Step 3: alphabetical order is ggplot2's default for text; the ranking is lost. Step 4: one function reorders the cities; the data are unchanged. Step 5: the title states the finding (London, Constantinople, and Paris are the only cities above 500,000). Step 6: the theme does not change any data. Wednesday's version also sized the dots by Playfair's circle area (size = area); that is one more aesthetic.

???

Two and a half minutes (24 to 26.5). The rule: inside aes() means "use this column"; outside aes() means "use this value for every mark". Step 1: color now carries data, so there is a legend. Step 2: a scale changes how the mapping is drawn, not what is mapped; Dark2 is a ColorBrewer qualitative palette (the slide from Part 1). Step 3: one constant color, no legend. Step 4: the mistake everyone makes once: the hex code becomes a one-value variable and ggplot2's default red-orange appears. If you ever see a legend with one entry that is your color code, this is why.

<script>
(function () {
  // Coach widget (Your Answer tab): sends the student's text to the game server's /api/coach.
  // A ?coach= query on the deck URL points it at another server (for testing); the default is production.
  var PROD = 'https://isa401-game-day.vercel.app/api/coach';
  var MSG = { keep_going: 'Keep going.', more_detail: 'Add more detail.', revisit: 'Revisit an idea.', done: 'All the key ideas are there.',
              busy: 'Many people are checking at once. Try again in a few seconds.',
              down: 'The checker is unavailable right now. Compare with the Answer tab.',
              short: 'Write a little more, then pause.', checking: 'Checking...', wait: 'Checking when you pause...',
              start: 'Start typing. Your answer is checked when you pause.' };
  function coachUrl() {
    var o = null;
    try { o = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('coach'); } catch (e) { o = null; }
    if (!o) { return PROD; }
    if (o.indexOf('http') !== 0) { return PROD; }
    if (o.indexOf('/api/coach') !== -1) { return o; }
    return o.replace(/[/]$/, '') + '/api/coach';
  }
  function load(k) { try { return window.localStorage.getItem(k) || ''; } catch (e) { return ''; } }
  function keep(k, v) { try { window.localStorage.setItem(k, v); } catch (e) {} }
  function build(root) {
    if (root.getAttribute('data-built')) { return; }
    root.setAttribute('data-built', '1');
    var ta = root.querySelector('.coach-ta'), status = root.querySelector('.coach-status');
    var go = root.querySelector('.coach-go'), chips = root.querySelector('.coach-chips'), hint = root.querySelector('.coach-hint');
    var act = root.getAttribute('data-activity'), key = root.getAttribute('data-store');
    // seq numbers each request; a response is used only if no newer request was sent (stale ones are dropped).
    // lastSent is the normalized text of the last request, so an unchanged answer is not sent again.
    var seq = 0, timer = null, openHint = -1, lastSent = '', pending = false, shown = null;
    function say(text, cls, keepIt) {
      status.textContent = text; status.className = 'coach-status ' + (cls || '');
      if (keepIt) { shown = [text, cls || '']; }
    }
    function norm(t) { return t.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, ' '); }
    function drawChips(ideas) {
      chips.textContent = '';
      ideas.forEach(function (idea, i) {
        var c = document.createElement('span');
        c.className = idea.met ? 'coach-chip met' : 'coach-chip';
        var lab = document.createElement('span');
        lab.textContent = idea.met ? (idea.label || ('Idea ' + (i + 1))) : ('Idea ' + (i + 1));
        c.appendChild(lab);
        if (!idea.met) {
          if (idea.hint) {
            var q = document.createElement('button');
            q.type = 'button'; q.textContent = '?'; q.title = 'Show a hint';
            q.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Hint for idea ' + (i + 1));
            q.addEventListener('click', function () {
              if (openHint === i) { openHint = -1; hint.textContent = ''; hint.className = 'coach-hint'; return; }
              openHint = i; hint.textContent = 'Hint for idea ' + (i + 1) + ': ' + idea.hint; hint.className = 'coach-hint on';
            });
            c.appendChild(q);
          }
        }
        chips.appendChild(c);
      });
    }
    function blank() {
      var n = Number(root.getAttribute('data-ideas')) || 4, a = [];
      for (var i = 0; i !== n; i = i + 1) { a.push({ met: false }); }
      drawChips(a);
    }
    function paint(v) {
      var ideas = Array.isArray(v.ideas) ? v.ideas : [];
      if (ideas.length) { drawChips(ideas); }
      openHint = -1; hint.textContent = ''; hint.className = 'coach-hint';
      if (v.status === 'done') { say(MSG.done, 'done', true); return; }
      say(v.note || MSG[v.status] || MSG.keep_going, v.status === 'revisit' ? 'revisit' : 'going', true);
    }
    function failed(msg, mine) {
      if (mine !== seq) { return; }
      pending = false; lastSent = '';
      say(msg, 'err', true);
    }
    function check(force) {
      clearTimeout(timer);
      var text = ta.value.trim(), n = norm(text);
      if (!(text.length >= 15)) { say(text ? MSG.short : MSG.start, '', true); return; }
      if (n === lastSent) {
        if (force !== true) {
          if (pending) { say(MSG.checking, 'checking'); } else { if (shown) { say(shown[0], shown[1]); } }
          return;
        }
      }
      lastSent = n; seq = seq + 1; pending = true;
      var mine = seq;
      say(MSG.checking, 'checking');
      fetch(coachUrl(), { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' }, body: JSON.stringify({ activity: act, text: text }) })
        .then(function (r) {
          if (mine !== seq) { return null; }
          if (r.status === 429) { failed(MSG.busy, mine); return null; }
          if (!r.ok) { failed(MSG.down, mine); return null; }
          return r.json();
        })
        .then(function (v) {
          if (!v) { return; }
          if (mine !== seq) { return; }
          pending = false;
          paint(v);
        })
        .catch(function () { failed(MSG.down, mine); });
    }
    ta.value = load(key);
    blank();
    say(MSG.start, '', true);
    if (ta.value.trim()) { say('Your saved answer is back. Press Check my answer.', '', true); }
    ta.addEventListener('input', function () {
      keep(key, ta.value);
      clearTimeout(timer);
      say(MSG.wait, 'checking');
      timer = setTimeout(check, 900);
    });
    go.addEventListener('click', function () { check(true); });
    ['keydown', 'keypress', 'keyup'].forEach(function (t) { root.addEventListener(t, function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); });
    ta.addEventListener('focus', function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.pause(); } });
    ta.addEventListener('blur', function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.resume(); } });
  }
  function buildAll() { document.querySelectorAll('.coach').forEach(build); }
  buildAll();
  if (window.slideshow) { if (!window.coachHooked) { window.coachHooked = true; window.slideshow.on('afterShowSlide', buildAll); } }
})();
</script>

???

Four and a half minutes (28.5 to 33): four on the timer, then the answer. No R typing; students describe the chart in words. The Your Answer tab checks their text with the game server's coach (Jev) while they type: four idea chips (data, aesthetics, geometry, facets) turn green when an idea is there, and the "?" on an unmet chip shows a hint. If the checker is down, the tab says so and students compare with the Answer tab. For testing, add ?coach=http://127.0.0.1:4030 to the deck URL. Accept any wording that names the right column for each channel. The detail that surprises people: the data have each penguin four times, once per panel, because the facets split the rows by palette and vision. The color column already holds the simulated colors, so the scale uses them as they are (scale_color_identity).

Step 2: every change is one layer: aesthetics (date order, highlight), geometry (value labels), scales (colors, commas), labels (a title that states the finding), theme. # Part 3: Game Day at Yager

```{r data_part345, include=FALSE}
# ---- Part 4: Exam 01 item analysis (Canvas export; exams graded as of Oct 14, 2026) ----
# Only the score range and percent of points per question are shown. No median, mean, or counts.
ia = readr::read_csv("../../docs/assignments/Exam 01/results/exam01_item_analysis_graded_as_of_2026-10-14.csv",
                     show_col_types = FALSE)
ex_hi = ia$QuizHighScore[1]
ex_lo = ia$QuizLowScore[1]
stopifnot(ex_lo == 42, ex_hi == 100)
items = ia |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Title)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * MeanEarnedPoints / PossiblePoints) |>
  dplyr::arrange(pct)
stopifnot(nrow(items) == 13, sum(items$PossiblePoints) == 25)
low3 = items |> dplyr::slice(1:3)
stopifnot(identical(low3$Title, c("Q1: Penguins", "Q12: LLMs and private data", "Q11: Extracting structure from text")))
# the exam's own question titles (the Canvas export uses short names)
ex_title = c("Q1: What is one row?", "Q12: LLMs and private data", "Q11: Extracting structure from text")
ex_pct = function(title) round(items$pct[items$Title == title])
ex_pts = function(title) items$PossiblePoints[items$Title == title]

# Q12: share of graded exams with full credit, and the most common partial score
q12 = jsonlite::fromJSON(items$AnswerFrequencies[items$Title == "Q12: LLMs and private data"])$scores
q12_full = sum(q12$count[q12$score == 1]) / sum(q12$count)
q12_part = q12[q12$score > 0 & q12$score < 1, ]
q12_mode = q12_part$score[which.max(q12_part$count)]
stopifnot(q12_full < 0.5, q12_mode == 0.5)

# ---- Q1: penguin captures (the exam file) ----
penguins = readr::read_csv("../../data/penguin_captures.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
q1_rows = penguins |> dplyr::count(species)
q1_birds = penguins |> dplyr::distinct(species, band) |> dplyr::count(species)
rows_of = function(s) q1_rows$n[q1_rows$species == s]
birds_of = function(s) q1_birds$n[q1_birds$species == s]
stopifnot(nrow(penguins) == 344,
          rows_of("Adelie") == 152, rows_of("Gentoo") == 124, rows_of("Chinstrap") == 68,
          birds_of("Adelie") == 80, birds_of("Gentoo") == 95, birds_of("Chinstrap") == 45,
          sum(q1_birds$n) == 220, dplyr::n_distinct(penguins$band) == 220,
          q1_birds$species[which.max(q1_birds$n)] == "Gentoo",
          max(table(penguins$band)) == 3)
q1_code = "penguins |> dplyr::distinct(species, band) |> dplyr::count(species)"
q1_out = paste(utils::capture.output(print(eval(parse(text = q1_code)))), collapse = "\n")
# five real rows: one band captured in three years and one band captured in two years
caps = penguins |> dplyr::add_count(band, name = "captures")
b3 = caps |> dplyr::filter(captures == 3) |> dplyr::arrange(band) |> dplyr::slice(1)
b2 = caps |> dplyr::filter(captures == 2, species != b3$species) |> dplyr::arrange(band) |> dplyr::slice(1)
five = penguins |>
  dplyr::filter(band %in% c(b3$band, b2$band)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(band, c(b3$band, b2$band)), year) |>
  dplyr::select(band, species, island, year, body_mass)
stopifnot(nrow(five) == 5)
five_html = five |>
  dplyr::mutate(band = ifelse(band == b3$band,
                              paste0("<b style='color:#c3142d;'>", band, "</b>"),
                              paste0("<b style='color:#0072B2;'>", band, "</b>"))) |>
  tbl(align = c("l", "l", "l", "r", "r"))
```

# Q11: Name the Model

<div class="qbar" style="margin-top:6px;"><b>The question.</b> ChatGPT's ellmer code does not run with the class key. Why not, and which one line fixes it?</div>

<div class="q11" style="display:grid; grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr; gap:14px; margin-top:10px;">
<div class="card"><div class="ch gray">As written</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:15px;">
`r hl_r('chat <- ellmer::chat_openai()', "80%")`
No model is named, so ellmer uses its default model. The class key only allows the class model, so a call that names no model is refused.
</div></div>
<div class="card"><div class="ch">The fix</div><div class="cb" style="font-size:15px;">
`r hl_r('chat <- ellmer::chat_openai(model = "gpt-5.6-luna")', "80%")`
With the class model named, the code runs and returns the listing's fields: a mansion that sleeps 19, with 9 bedrooms.
</div></div>
</div>

<div class="lesson" style="margin-top:16px;"><b class="r">When code fails, look for a default you did not choose.</b> Here it was the model. If ChatGPT's code ran as written for you, there was no fault to find, and you received full credit.</div>

???

Four and a half minutes (71.5 to 76). Per the answer key, the failure depends on the class key being limited to the class model; anyone whose code ran as written received full credit for the question.

# Summary of Main Points

By now, you should be able to do the following:

- **Apply** the grammar of graphics using ggplot2: every chart has data, aesthetics, and a geometry; facets, statistics, coordinates, scales, and a theme are added with <b>+</b> and have defaults.

- **Map** data types to visual encodings in code: a column inside aes() is mapped to a channel, a value outside aes() is set for every mark, and the color scale should match the data type (qualitative for nominal data, sequential or diverging for ordered values).

- **Refine** charts with labels, scales, and themes: a title that states the finding, axis labels with units, direct labels where they help, and a theme for the parts that do not show data.

- **Critique** and improve draft visualizations by changing one layer at a time, and check what one row is before you count or chart it.

???

One minute (78 to 79). One bullet per learning objective. The last bullet ties the grammar to the exam review: checking what a row is comes before any chart.

<script>
(function () {
  // Password gate for the answer boxes (class answer-gate). The password is fall2026; case and spaces are ignored.
  // Light gate only: the password is stored as a 32-bit FNV-1a hash so it is not readable in
  // the page source, but anyone determined can open the box from DevTools. sessionStorage
  // remembers an unlock for the rest of the browser session, so one password opens every box.
  var HASH = "806d8122";
  var KEY = "isa401_gate_16";
  function fnv(str) {
    var x = 0x811c9dc5;
    for (var i = 0; i !== str.length; i = i + 1) { x ^= str.charCodeAt(i); x = Math.imul(x, 16777619) >>> 0; }
    return ("0000000" + x.toString(16)).slice(-8);
  }
  function unlocked() { try { return sessionStorage.getItem(KEY) === "1"; } catch (e) { return false; } }
  function remember() { try { sessionStorage.setItem(KEY, "1"); } catch (e) {} }

  function arm(d) {
    if (d.getAttribute("data-gated")) { return; }
    d.setAttribute("data-gated", "1");
    var prompt = null;
    d.addEventListener("toggle", function () {
      if (!d.open) { return; }   // closing (including our own d.open = false below) needs nothing
      if (unlocked()) { if (prompt) { prompt.remove(); prompt = null; } return; }
      d.open = false;
      if (prompt) { prompt.querySelector("input").focus(); return; }
      prompt = document.createElement("div");
      prompt.setAttribute("style", "display:flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; margin:6px 0 0 0; font-size:13px;");
      prompt.innerHTML = "<span style='color:#585E60;'>Password</span>" +
        "<input type='password' autocomplete='off' style='font-family:Source Code Pro, monospace; font-size:13px; padding:4px 8px; border:1px solid #d1d5db; border-radius:6px; width:140px;'>" +
        "<button type='button' style='background:#c3142d; color:#fff; border:0; border-radius:6px; padding:5px 14px; font-weight:700; font-size:13px; cursor:pointer;'>Unlock</button>" +
        "<span class='gate-msg' style='color:#c3142d;'></span>";
      d.parentNode.insertBefore(prompt, d.nextSibling);
      var input = prompt.querySelector("input");
      var msg = prompt.querySelector(".gate-msg");
      // keep remark's keyboard shortcuts (f, p, digits) from firing while typing: same
      // pause/resume pattern xaringanExtra uses for its editable fields
      ["keydown", "keypress", "keyup"].forEach(function (t) { input.addEventListener(t, function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); });
      input.addEventListener("focus", function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.pause(); } });
      input.addEventListener("blur", function () { if (window.slideshow) { window.slideshow.resume(); } });
      function tryIt() {
        if (fnv(input.value.toLowerCase().split(" ").join("")) === HASH) { remember(); prompt.remove(); prompt = null; d.open = true; }
        else { msg.textContent = "Not it."; input.select(); }
      }
      prompt.querySelector("button").addEventListener("click", tryIt);
      input.addEventListener("keydown", function (e) { if (e.key === "Enter") { tryIt(); } });
      input.focus();
    });
  }
  function armAll() { document.querySelectorAll("details.answer-gate").forEach(arm); }
  armAll();
  if (window.slideshow) { if (!window.answerGateHooked) { window.answerGateHooked = true; window.slideshow.on("afterShowSlide", armAll); } }
})();
</script>
